newsitem.title: USA: FERC approves Southern Natural pipeline expansion.
newsitem.headline: FERC approves Southern Natural pipeline expansion.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday approved a plan by Sonat Inc's Southern Natural Gas Co to expand its pipeline system to serve customers in Alabama and Georgia.

The controversial plan to build about 120 miles of new natural gas pipeline has stirred opposition from landowners in northern Alabama and would involve going through or underneath a national wildlife refuge.
Before the company can begin construction, it must receive a green light from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and landowners who have yet to allow surveys on their property.
The commission recommended that the pipeline be built beneath Wheeler National Wildlife Refuge instead of alongside Interstate-65 in the refuge.
Using the existing right-of-way next to I-65 would harm wetlands and the Tennessee River, where there are several threatened or endangered species, the FERC said in its environmental statement.
The commission said an alternative pipeline proposal by Southern Natural's competitor Alabama-Tennessee Natural Gas Co would be less environmentally damaging.

But FERC rejected Alabama-Tennessee's plan because the company had not yet secured any customers for its project, and two of its biggest customers, Huntsville Utilities Gas System and Decatur Utilities, had opted to shift to Southern Natural's system when its expansion is complete.

The commission ordered Alabama-Tennessee to extend service to Huntsville and Decatur for one year, because Southern Natural's expansion will not be ready to serve the two municipal utilities when their existing contracts with Alabama-Tennessee expire in November.
